sentiment.instructions: Judge the overall sentiment the tweet's author expresses or conveys: their attitude toward what they mention, their mood, or the clear good/bad nature of reported news. Label by evaluative tone, not topic; dates, events and celebrities alone are neutral.

criteria.positive: Author shows enthusiasm, liking, approval, hope, gratitude or praise, even mildly (impressed, sounds perfect, cool, love, can't wait, let's go, :) ), defends or compliments someone, or promotes/invites with upbeat wording (celebrate, win, who wants tickets, don't miss, come support, please share). Also reported wins and achievements (beats X, reaches final, wins title), condolences with prayers or blessings (RIP, may God bless), well-wishing.
criteria.neutral: Factual reports and news without a clear good/bad slant, event notices giving only logistics (register, RSVP, info session, meeting at 6pm), spam, questions, requests or pleas to celebrities, hedged guesses (may be, could be), live sports updates. Also laughing banter and jokes about celebrities or sports (lol, lmao, bwahaha), and mixed feelings where positive and negative balance.
criteria.negative: Author shows displeasure: anger, sadness, disappointment, disgust, dread, boredom or contempt, including complaints about their own situation (going to die, ugh, I miss, not because I enjoy it), grumbling about products or services, sarcastic or insinuating criticism (perhaps a bit insensitive, #justsaying), pointed political/religious criticism or rhetorical challenges, insults, wishing harm. Also reports of bad events: attacks, bombings, deaths, crimes, arrests, losses, scandals, injuries, failures.
